topic: Islam: The Four Rightly Guided Caliphs
subject: religious-studies

moments.title: First sermon at Sarnath
moments.body: The Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta ('Setting the Wheel of Dharma in Motion') is delivered in the Deer Park at Sarnath. The Buddha teaches the Four Noble Truths: there is dukkha (suffering, unsatisfactoriness); the cause is craving (tanha); cessation is possible; the Noble Eightfold Path leads there.
moments.takeaway: The Eightfold Path: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration. The 'middle way' between asceticism and indulgence.

moments.title: Pali Canon written
moments.body: Around 100 BCE, the Buddhist teachings — preserved orally for 400 years — are first written down at Aluvihara in Sri Lanka, possibly during a famine that threatened the chain of oral transmission. The Tipitaka (Three Baskets) contains Vinaya (monastic discipline), Sutta (discourses), and Abhidhamma (philosophical analysis).
moments.takeaway: The Pali Canon remains the canonical scriptures for Theravada Buddhism. Mahayana traditions added many more sutras (Lotus, Heart, Diamond, Pure Land).

moments.title: Engaged Buddhism
moments.who: Thich Nhat Hanh, the Dalai Lama, B.R. Ambedkar
moments.body: Thich Nhat Hanh's 'Engaged Buddhism' (term coined 1960s) applies Buddhist principles to social action. B.R. Ambedkar leads the Dalit mass conversion to Buddhism in 1956. The 14th Dalai Lama goes into Indian exile in 1959 and becomes a global figure.
moments.takeaway: Modern Buddhism has had to engage colonialism, modernity, science, and political conflict in ways the early sangha didn't anticipate.

now.title: Buddhism in the modern world
now.body: Around 500 million Buddhists globally. Mindfulness practices (MBSR, MBCT) have entered mainstream Western healthcare and education. Theravada (Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar), Mahayana (China, Japan, Korea, Vietnam) and Vajrayana (Tibet, Mongolia) all flourish in different forms. Secular Buddhism (Stephen Batchelor) is a growing tendency.
now.open_questions: What is the Buddha's actual teaching? Some scholars argue the Pali Canon's earliest material reaches close; others that all our texts are later compositions. The historical Buddha is harder to access than the textual Buddha.

reflection: The Four Noble Truths frame human life as a problem with a solution. The diagnosis (suffering caused by craving) and treatment (eightfold path) form a complete therapy. Their continued global appeal — across radically different cultural contexts — testifies to their depth.
